clue.text: Batting streak, reportedly to no avail

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the words built are heard rather than seen, so their sound gives the spelling

parts.note: a batsman who is batting is in; a vein is a streak of colour, as in marble

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator notes a run of good batting that ultimately achieved nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: IN VEIN, said out loud, matches the phrase entered.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe effort that produced no result, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Setter barking after spy leaves Tube station

indicators.note: after places the rearranged dog's name following the spy in the answer

parts.note: James Bond is the famous fictional spy

indicators.note: barking, meaning mad, signals that the letters of setter are scrambled

explanation.surface: A setter dog yaps as a secret agent departs from a London Underground stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the crossword compiler or the dog, but its letters are rearranged to STREET; 'leaves' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Bond Street is a stop on the London Underground, known as the Tube.

clue.text: Luxurious hotel's withdrawn credit

indicators.note: withdrawn says the hotel's letter is taken away from the word for luxurious

parts.note: plush means luxurious or opulent
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A posh hotel has taken back a guest's credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is something in one's favour, an asset or point counted to one's credit.

clue.text: Crowd supported Egypt's leader in rally

parts.note: a jam is a crowd packed tightly together
bore, past tense of bear, means supported or carried

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A throng backed the Egyptian head of state at a political rally.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamboree is a large festive gathering, like a scout rally.

clue.text: Working with ordinary couple of females intermittently

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
and means together with
F stands for female, so two of them give FF

explanation.surface: Someone works alongside a regular pair of women, but only sporadically.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens now and then, stopping and starting, is intermittent.

clue.text: Folly of new and old bridge partners seen playing

parts.note: in bridge, North and South play as partners

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of seen are in action and moved about

explanation.surface: Players at a bridge table, both novice and veteran, are seen acting foolishly.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players sit as North, South, East and West, and North and South are one partnership; 'playing' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Folly is foolish behaviour, and talking or acting nonsense is the same idea.

clue.text: Large sum of money bank employee gives palm reader?

parts.note: a fortune is a very large amount of money
a teller is a bank cashier who serves customers

explanation.surface: A bank cashier handing over a huge sum seems to be reading someone's hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows palm reading is just one example of the craft.
explanation.definitionFit: Palmistry is one method of predicting the future, so a palm reader is an example of a seer.

clue.text: Slowly describing a type of shed

indicators.note: describing in its sense of drawing around means the outer word encloses the a

parts.note: lento is the musical direction meaning slowly

explanation.surface: Someone slowly gives an account of a kind of garden hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shed built against a wall, its roof sloping one way.

clue.text: After tango, enjoy Blackpool, say

indicators.note: after puts the word for enjoy following the tango letter in the answer

parts.note: T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to own or enjoy something is to have it, as in enjoying good health

explanation.surface: After a tango dance, have a good time at a seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackpool is a seaside resort town in north-west England, famous for its ballroom dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackpool is one example of an English town, hence the 'say'.

clue.text: A Parisian's help not declared

parts.note: un is French for a, as a Parisian would say
the 's of the clue supplies the letter S
aid means help

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's assistance went unacknowledged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left unspoken or unstated has not been declared.

clue.text: Got up to deliver decorated dish as a prize, maybe

definitions.text: decorated dish as a prize, maybe

parts.note: rose, past tense of rise, means got up
in cricket, to bowl is to deliver the ball

explanation.surface: Someone stood to present an ornamented platter as an award.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose bowl is an ornamental bowl, often silver, frequently given as a trophy.

clue.text: Ate bun doubtfully during golf club spread

indicators.note: during places the jumbled letters within the golf club's name

parts.note: a putter is the golf club used on the green

indicators.note: doubtfully suggests the letters of ate bun are uncertain and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer warily eats a bun mid-round, putter in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' looks like a verb or a meal, but is the definition; 'doubtfully' scrambles the fodder and 'during' places it inside the club.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanut butter is a paste one spreads on bread, so it is a type of spread.

clue.text: What superstar expects ringing about one after lead?

indicators.note: about, meaning around, says the bell word encloses the other pieces

parts.note: tolling is the slow ringing of a bell

indicators.note: after puts the one following the lead symbol

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cryptic question about what a celebrity hopes for, with bells ringing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' is the metal, not leading role.
explanation.definitionFit: A star performer's name is printed largest and first on posters, the most prominent billing.

clue.text: Access for transport

definitions.meaning: a way in or admission to a place
to transport someone is to carry them away with delight, to enrapture

explanation.surface: A sign about getting in for vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is pronounced differently, with stress on the second syllable: to put into a trance.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorway gives access, and to enrapture someone is to carry them away in delight.

clue.text: Exploited American Democrat following first of elections

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An American Democrat feels taken advantage of after the first round of elections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' just places the Democrat's D after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit someone or something is to make use of them, often unfairly.

clue.text: Fat got from ducks, originally — excellent

indicators.note: originally means taking the letter the word begins with

parts.note: ripping is old British slang for excellent

explanation.surface: The fat that comes off roast duck is first-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: Dripping is the fat collected from roasting meat, used in British cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Dripping is the fat that runs from meat as it roasts, a specific kind of cooking fat.

clue.text: Appraise organ aloft

parts.note: the eye is the organ of sight
aloft means up high

explanation.surface: Assess the pipe organ in the gallery above.
explanation.definitionFit: To look someone over carefully, sizing them up, is to appraise them.

clue.text: Eagle inhabiting Alderney

indicators.note: inhabiting says the bird is living inside the island's name

explanation.surface: A sea eagle lives on Alderney.
explanation.walkthrough: Alderney is one of the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed sea eagle.

clue.text: Fully briefed, as one chosen by casting director may be?

definitions.meaning: fully informed and up to date

definitions.text: as one chosen by casting director may be?
definitions.meaning: an actor cast in a film literally appears in the movie

explanation.surface: An actor picked by a casting director is fully informed about the role.
explanation.definitionFit: Being kept informed is an idiom for being in the know; a cast actor is literally in the film.

clue.text: List of charges, the result of squabble about artist turning up

indicators.note: about, meaning around, says the quarrel word surrounds the artist

parts.note: a tiff is a petty squabble

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A price list sparked a row when a painter arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is the crossword's usual artist; 'turning up' reverses it in this down clue and 'about' wraps the quarrel round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a schedule of prices or duties, a published list of charges.

clue.text: Go slowly in tug

definitions.meaning: to haul or pull something along

explanation.surface: Move gently in a tugboat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: tedious time passes slowly, and to haul is to pull.

clue.text: Support very large gangster's suggestion

parts.note: a prop is a support
OS is short for outsize, very large in clothing sizes
Al Capone is the archetypal gangster

explanation.surface: Back the mob boss's big idea.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is part of the gangster leaf: it signals possession, not an extra S.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal is a plan put forward for consideration, i.e. a suggestion.

clue.text: Problem with head of shire horse

indicators.note: head of means the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a nag is an old or worn-out horse

explanation.surface: Trouble with the head of a shire horse, the heavy draught breed.
explanation.walkthrough: A shire horse is a large British draught breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is a hidden difficulty or catch, a problem.

clue.text: Sounds produced by this cat round a queen

indicators.note: round says the wild cat goes around the other letters

parts.note: the lynx is a wild cat
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A big cat purrs and growls circling a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The voice box in the throat produces the sounds of speech and song.

clue.text: A grand finale associated with ace programme

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
a finale is an end
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A spectacular finish marks a first-class show.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a schedule of items to be dealt with, a programme of business.

clue.text: Manage, at a later time, to set off in pursuit

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
after means afterwards, at a later time

explanation.surface: Organise things now, then later give chase.
explanation.definitionFit: To chase someone is to go off following them in pursuit.
